subject: general
question: Silicon doped with gallium forms ______.
solution:
The correct answer is a __**p-type semiconductor.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Silicon **doped with** gallium** forms a** p-type semiconducto**r because gallium is a** trivalent impurity** and replaces some of the silicon atoms in the crystal lattice, creating a** hole** in the valence band.
 
• **P-type semiconductors** have a **majority of holes** as their charge carriers and a smaller number of **electrons,** which are the minority carriers.
 
• **N-type semiconductors,** on the other hand, are doped with a **pentavalent impurity** like phosphorus, which adds an extra electron to the conduction band and creates a **surplus of electrons** as the majority carriers.
 
• **Superconductors **are materials that exhibit **zero electrical resistance **below a certain** temperature, **and **silicon doped with gallium** is not known to exhibit superconductivity.
 
• **Insulators **are materials that do not conduct electricity at all and have a **very high resistance,** which is not the case with **p-type semiconductors.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In a** p-type semiconductor**, the holes in the valence band can move from **one atom to another **and act as **positive charge carriers**, while the electrons in the conduction band are** immobile unless **excited by an external energy source. 
 
• The doping process is a way to intentionally introduce impurities into a **semiconductor crystal** to alter its electrical properties and enable the creation of **p-n junctions**, which are the basis of many **electronic devices.**
 
• Some common **p-type dopants** besides gallium are** boron and aluminum, **while common **n-type dopants** include **arsenic and antimony.**
 
• The properties of a semiconductor depend not only on its doping but also on its** temperature, light exposure**, and other environmental factors that can affect its **carrier concentration, mobility, and recombination.**
